sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module purpose and imports
sections.what: Describes what the file does: routes facts to one pillar and sub-driver, places findings, and scores projects. Brings in helpers and types.
sections.why: The header says it ports an earlier Python build script, so it should match that logic.
sections.watch_out: Changes to scoring here can make results differ from the original Python version.

sections.name: count
sections.title: Count keyword hits
sections.what: Counts how many times the keyword phrases appear in a text, including repeats.
sections.why: Likely reason: a simple way to score which pillar or sub-driver a text is about.
sections.watch_out: Keywords match inside longer words, so a short keyword such as gas can be counted inside another word.

sections.name: admit
sections.title: Admit or hold a fact
sections.what: Marks a fact as admitted, or holds it with a reason: off-project, not found on the source page, or no source recorded.
sections.why: Likely reason: only checked facts should reach the deck. The held reasons are written so readers can see why a fact was left out.
sections.watch_out: Any verification status other than unverified or unsourced is admitted, including any status not seen here.

sections.name: routeAndAssess (part 1)
sections.title: Route facts and place findings
sections.what: Gives each admitted fact one pillar and one sub-driver using a category map or keyword votes, and counts facts that are outcome evidence or unrouted. Then places each finding by its supporting facts (counted double) and keyword votes. A finding whose supporting facts were all held loses its pillar.
sections.why: The header explains the weights: facts count two and keywords count one.
sections.watch_out: A finding whose supporting facts were all held drops out of every pillar without any warning in the output.

sections.name: routeAndAssess: for
sections.title: Score each project against each pillar
sections.what: For each project and pillar, counts strength, risk or watch, and neutral findings, then scores the cell as strength, risk, mixed, neutral or not applicable. Then builds the pillar summaries: cell counts, sub-driver fact lists, and good, caution and neutral finding lists.
sections.why: The header says cells are scored from finding stances, never from project outcome.
sections.watch_out: Because outcomes are kept out of scoring, a delivered project with risk findings still shows risk.

sections.name: discrimination
sections.title: Pillar discrimination index
sections.what: Calculates how well a pillar separates delivered projects from overrun or cautionary ones. Gives a label of discriminating, weak or inverse, or insufficient sample when fewer than three projects fall in either group.
sections.why: The comment defines the index and the sample rule.
sections.watch_out: The labels use fixed thresholds of 0.3 and 0, so small threshold changes change the labels without changing the calculation.

summary: Routes each fact and finding to one pillar, scores each project against each pillar, and measures how well each pillar separates successful projects from troubled ones.
purpose: Turn raw facts and analyst findings into a pillar-by-project picture that the recipe deck can show.
why: The header says this is a port of an earlier Python build step, so it keeps the same logic. The intent that cell scores come from finding stances rather than project outcome is stated in the header.
how: First, admit each fact or hold it with a reason. Second, assign each admitted fact one pillar and one sub-driver, using a category map first and keyword votes second. Third, place each finding by the pillars of its supporting facts, counted double, plus keyword votes. Fourth, score each project against each pillar from its finding stances. Fifth, summarise each pillar. Last, compute the discrimination index.
inputs: The framework (pillars, sub-drivers, keywords and category map), the list of projects, the facts, and the findings.
outputs: An assessment with a project-by-pillar score matrix, a summary for each pillar, counts of unrouted and outcome-only facts, and counts of how each fact was routed.
risks: Keyword voting can put a fact in the wrong pillar. Weights and thresholds are hand-set. A finding whose supporting facts are all held loses its pillar without any warning. Changing how stances map to scores changes every recipe.
debug: Check a fact's admitted flag and held reason first. Then check its pillar and sub-driver. For an odd project score, look at that project's finding stances in the matrix. If numbers differ from the original Python logic, compare the two.
